record.title: Throttling is concerned about the sum of the size of a zero forcing set and the associated propagation time, i.e.
record.statement: Throttling is concerned about the sum of the size of a zero forcing set and the associated propagation time, i.e. we are willing to not use the minimum zero forcing number if it decreases the propagation time, in other words if $B$ is a zero forcing set and $\text{pt}(G,B)$ is the corresponding propagation time then the throttling number is $\min\{|B| + \text{pt}(G,B) \}$.
record.source_name: AimPL: Zero forcing and its applications (posed by Chassidy Bozeman)

record.title: Equi-isoclinic subspaces
record.statement:
Let $N_\alpha^k(d)$ be the maximum number of $k$-dimensional subspaces of $\mathbb{R}^d$, every pair of which is equi-isoclinic with angle $\alpha$. Then 

(1) $N_{\alpha}^k(d)=O_{\alpha,k}(d)$. 

(2) $N_{\alpha}^k(d)=O_{k}(d)+o_{\alpha,k}(d)$.
record.source_name: AimPL: High-dimensional phenomena in discrete analysis (posed by Yufei Zhao)

record.title: Graph Theory Motivated Questions (problem 3)
record.statement: Let $G = (V,E)$ be a graph of maximum degree $\Delta$. Let $\chi(t)$ be the chromatic polynomial (i.e. $\chi(q)$ is the number of ways of properly coloring the graph $G$ with $q$ colors). Then, is $\chi(t) \neq 0$ for any $t \in {\\mathbb{C}}$ so that $|t| > 2\Delta$. Also if the real part of $\text{Re }t > \Delta + 1$, then do we have $\chi(t) \neq 0$?
record.source_name: AimPL: The geometry of polynomials in combinatorics and sampling
